---
name: visualize
description: >-
  Turn data, concepts, or processes into a polished standalone visualization —
  chart, table, diagram, dashboard, KPI scorecard, timeline, or explainer —
  written as self-contained code, saved locally, and exported to an image at a
  16:9 aspect ratio by default (any ratio on request). Use whenever the user
  wants to visualize, chart, graph, plot, diagram, or "show" numbers / metrics /
  a report / a comparison / a breakdown / a trend / a timeline / a flow; pastes a
  report or table and wants it turned into a graphic; or asks for an infographic,
  dashboard, scorecard, or a shareable picture of data. Also use for "make this a
  visual", "render this", "turn this into a chart/graph", or "export a diagram".
  Do NOT use for editing existing raster images (photo retouching), for a plain
  in-conversation markdown table with no image export, for live embedded app UI
  components (use a frontend skill), or for full slide decks (use pptx).
---

# Visualize

Turn an input — pasted data, a report, a set of numbers, a concept, or a process — into a single, polished visualization, saved as self-contained code and exported to an image at **16:9 by default** (any aspect ratio on request).

The design ethos is borrowed from generative UI: read the input, pick the *right* representation (don't default to a bar chart for everything), and render one self-contained artifact that looks intentional, not auto-generated.

## What every run produces

Inside `./visualizations/<slug>/` (relative to the user's working directory unless they give a path):

- `index.html` — the self-contained source (open in any browser, edit by hand)
- `<slug>.png` — the rendered image, **1600×900 (16:9) at 2× scale** by default

Always end by telling the user both paths and surfacing the PNG.

## Workflow

Follow these in order. Each step links to detail only where you need it.

### 1. Read the input and choose the representation

Match the input to a representation using the decision matrix below. The single most common mistake is reaching for a bar chart when the data wants something else — a few big numbers want a **KPI scorecard**, a part-to-whole wants a **donut**, a ranking wants **horizontal bars**, a process wants a **diagram**, raw rows want a **styled table**. Pick deliberately.

| The input is… | Best representation | How to build it |
|---|---|---|
| A few headline numbers / metrics | KPI scorecard (big-number cards) | HTML + CSS |
| Categories compared in size / a ranking | Bar chart (vertical or horizontal) | inline SVG |
| A value changing over time / a trend | Line or area chart | inline SVG |
| Parts of a whole (≤6 slices) | Donut / pie + legend | inline SVG |
| Several series across periods (daily/weekly/monthly) | Grouped bars or small multiples, or a scorecard + bars combo | inline SVG + CSS grid |
| Rows of structured records | Styled data table | HTML + CSS |
| A two-variable relationship | Scatter / bubble | inline SVG |
| A process, flow, pipeline, or architecture | Diagram (nodes + connectors) | inline SVG |
| A sequence of dated events | Timeline | inline SVG + CSS |
| Hierarchy / nesting | Treemap or indented tree | inline SVG |
| An abstract concept needing explanation | Annotated explainer (labels + arrows over a diagram) | HTML + SVG |
| Genuinely interactive *code* deliverable, or 100+ data points | Chart.js (escalation) | CDN, see recipes |
| 3D scene | Three.js (escalation) | CDN, see recipes |

When the input has multiple natural cuts (e.g. the social-analytics example with Daily / Weekly / Monthly across platforms), prefer **one composed layout** — a header KPI row plus a small set of comparison charts — over three disconnected charts. A dashboard reads as one artifact; three loose charts read as three.

**Default to inline SVG + HTML/CSS.** It renders pixel-crisp at any resolution, needs no network, and never half-draws during export. Only escalate to Chart.js / Three.js when interactivity in the *openable HTML* or sheer data volume genuinely calls for it (see `references/recipes.md`).

### 2. Set up the output folder

Pick a short kebab-case `<slug>` from the subject (e.g. `social-analytics`, `q4-revenue`, `auth-flow`). Create `./visualizations/<slug>/`.

### 3. Author `index.html`

Start from the template — it gives you a correct 16:9 stage, light/dark theming, web-safe typography, and the export-ready signal already wired:

```
cp <this-skill>/assets/stage.html ./visualizations/<slug>/index.html
```

Then fill it in (the template has labelled `FILL:` regions):

- **Title / subtitle / source** — a real headline, not "Chart". Include the period or date range if the data has one. Put any attribution in the footer slot.
- **The viz** — replace the `#viz` region with your representation. Build charts as inline SVG using the recipes; lay out scorecards/tables with CSS grid/flex.
- **The data** — transcribe the user's numbers *exactly*. Double-check every figure against the input; wrong numbers make the whole artifact worthless. Don't invent data to fill space.
- **Signal ready** — call `vizReady()` once the final frame is painted (the template auto-calls it after fonts load + two animation frames, so you only need to call it manually if you draw asynchronously, e.g. a Chart.js `onComplete`).

Design bar (see `references/recipes.md` for the full checklist and snippets):

- Fill the stage — no large empty margins, no tiny chart marooned in a sea of background.
- Type scales with the stage using `clamp()` / `cqmin` units (already set up), so it stays legible at any export size.
- A restrained palette: one accent hue + neutrals, or the provided categorical ramp. Avoid rainbow defaults.
- Label directly where you can (value labels on bars, end-of-line labels) instead of forcing the eye to a distant axis.
- Whitespace, alignment, and a clear visual hierarchy (title → key numbers → supporting detail) do most of the work.

### 4. Export to an image

From the visualization folder (or anywhere, with absolute paths):

```
node <this-skill>/scripts/render.mjs --in index.html --out <slug>.png
```

Default output is **1600×900 @2× (16:9)**. The aspect ratio is fully modifiable:

```
# A square for Instagram
node <this-skill>/scripts/render.mjs --in index.html --out sq.png --aspect 1:1 --width 1080

# A tall story / phone frame
node <this-skill>/scripts/render.mjs --in index.html --out story.png --aspect 9:16 --width 1080

# Exact pixels
node <this-skill>/scripts/render.mjs --in index.html --out big.png --width 2560 --height 1440

# Transparent background, dark theme
node <this-skill>/scripts/render.mjs --in index.html --out t.png --bg transparent --theme dark
```

Flags: `--aspect` (`16:9` default, `4:3`, `1:1`, `9:16`, `21:9`, `3:2`, `2:1`), `--width`/`--height` (px; give either with `--aspect`, or both for exact), `--scale` (DPI multiplier, default `2`), `--theme` (`light`|`dark`), `--bg` (`white`|`transparent`|`#hex`). Full reference: `references/recipes.md`.

The stage fills the viewport, so one `index.html` exports cleanly at any ratio. For a *drastically* different ratio (e.g. designing for 16:9 then exporting 9:16), glance at the result and re-tune the layout if elements crowd or strand — don't assume a 16:9 composition is automatically good as a vertical.

### 5. Deliver

Confirm the PNG was written, then report the saved `index.html` and `.png` paths and surface the image to the user. If the render step failed, see Troubleshooting before reporting success — never claim an image exists without confirming the file.

## Troubleshooting the render

`render.mjs` tries, in order: Playwright with installed Chrome/Edge, then Playwright's bundled Chromium, then a system Chrome/Chromium/Edge/Brave binary directly. One of these is present on most machines. If all fail it prints the exact fix; relay it. The usual one-time install:

```
npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium
```

If a chart exports half-drawn or blank, the ready signal didn't fire before capture — make sure asynchronous drawing calls `vizReady()` on completion, or pass `--wait 8000` to give it more time.

## Reference

- `references/recipes.md` — copy-paste SVG/CSS recipes (bar, line, area, donut, scatter, KPI cards, table, diagram, timeline), the Chart.js / Three.js escalation patterns, the full design checklist, and every `render.mjs` flag.
- `assets/stage.html` — the 16:9 stage template you copy in step 3.

{
  "skill_name": "visualize",
  "evals": [
    {
      "id": 0,
      "name": "social-analytics-dashboard",
      "prompt": "Turn this into a visual I can share:\n\nSocial analytics report\n\nDaily (2026-06-15)\n• X: Atai 1,397 | CopilotKit 3,892 | Other 43\n• LinkedIn: CopilotKit 9,149\n\nWeekly (2026-06-09 → 2026-06-15)\n• X: Atai 20,352 | CopilotKit 33,613 | Other 1,079\n• LinkedIn: CopilotKit 20,349\n\nMonthly (2026-05-17 → 2026-06-15)\n• X: Atai 595,670 | CopilotKit 162,176 | Other 36,125\n• LinkedIn: CopilotKit 63,500",
      "expected_output": "A self-contained HTML file plus a 16:9 PNG, saved locally under a visualizations/ folder. The graphic should read as one composed dashboard (KPI numbers + comparison chart and/or table) covering the Daily/Weekly/Monthly timeframes across X and LinkedIn, with every figure transcribed exactly.",
      "files": [],
      "assertions": [
        "Both an HTML source file and a PNG image were saved under a visualizations/ directory",
        "The exported PNG has a 16:9 aspect ratio (width/height within 1% of 1.7778)",
        "The visualization renders the data graphically (contains an <svg> chart, a <table>, and/or KPI number cards) rather than just restating the text",
        "Key figures from the input appear verbatim in the HTML, including 9,149 / 33,613 / 595,670 / 63,500",
        "The three timeframes (Daily, Weekly, Monthly) and both platforms (X, LinkedIn) are distinguishable in the output"
      ]
    },
    {

      "name": "revenue-bars-square",
      "prompt": "Quick one for the board deck — turn our Q4 revenue into a chart. By region: North America $4.2M, EMEA $3.1M, APAC $2.8M, LATAM $0.9M. Can you make it square so it drops cleanly onto the slide?",
      "expected_output": "A self-contained HTML file plus a PNG exported at a 1:1 (square) aspect ratio, saved locally. The four regions should be shown as a bar chart (vertical or horizontal ranking) with exact values and a clear title.",
      "files": [],
      "assertions": [
        "Both an HTML source file and a PNG image were saved locally",
        "The exported PNG is square (width equals height, within 1%) as requested",
        "All four regions (North America, EMEA, APAC, LATAM) and their values ($4.2M, $3.1M, $2.8M, $0.9M) are present",
        "The data is rendered as a real graphical chart — SVG bars (<rect>), donut/pie arcs (<circle>/stroke-dasharray), or a chart <canvas> — not as plain text"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": 2,
      "name": "request-flow-diagram",
      "prompt": "Can you visualize the request flow in our app for the architecture doc? A client hits the API gateway, the gateway calls the auth service to validate the token, then it queries our Postgres database, and the response flows back out to the client. I'd like a clean diagram, not a chart.",
      "expected_output": "A self-contained HTML file plus a 16:9 PNG, saved locally. The output should be a node-and-connector flow diagram (boxes for client, API gateway, auth service, Postgres, connected by arrows) — NOT a bar/line/pie chart.",
      "files": [],
      "assertions": [
        "Both an HTML source file and a PNG image were saved locally",
        "The exported PNG has a 16:9 aspect ratio (width/height within 1% of 1.7778)",
        "The output is a diagram with connectors (SVG containing arrow markers or lines linking labeled nodes), not a bar/line/pie chart",
        "All four components are labeled: client, API gateway, auth service, and Postgres/database"
      ]
    }

}

# Visualization recipes Copy-paste building blocks for the `#viz` region of `assets/stage.html`. Everything here is inline SVG + HTML/CSS — no dependencies, crisp at any export resolution, fully offline. Chart.js / Three.js escalation patterns are at the end. All snippets assume the stage template's tokens (`--ink`, `--muted`, `--line`, `--accent`, `--c1`…`--c6`) and helper classes (`.panel`, `.grid`, `.kpi`, `table.data`, `svg.chart`). ## Contents - [Design checklist](#design-checklist) — read before building - [Color & palette](#color--palette) - [KPI scorecard](#kpi-scorecard) - [Bar chart — vertical](#bar-chart--vertical) - [Bar chart — horizontal / ranking](#bar-chart--horizontal--ranking) - [Grouped bars](#grouped-bars) - [Line / area chart](#line--area-chart) - [Donut / pie](#donut--pie) - [Scatter](#scatter) - [Data table](#data-table) - [Process / flow diagram](#process--flow-diagram) - [Timeline](#timeline) - [Composing a dashboard](#composing-a-dashboard) - [Escalation: Chart.js](#escalation-chartjs) - [Escalation: Three.js](#escalation-threejs) - [render.mjs flag reference](#rendermjs-flag-reference) --- ## Design checklist Before exporting, sanity-check: - **Right representation.** Re-read the decision matrix in SKILL.md. A bar chart is rarely the only option. - **Numbers are exact.** Every value matches the source input. No invented data, no rounded-away precision unless the source was already rounded. - **Fills the stage.** No chart stranded in a sea of empty background; no clipping at the edges. Use the full width/height of `#viz`. - **Direct labels.** Put values on/next to bars, points, and line ends. Axes are a fallback, not the primary read. - **One accent + neutrals**, or the categorical ramp in order. No rainbow-by-default. - **Hierarchy.** Title → headline numbers → supporting chart → source. The eye should land on what matters first. - **Legible at size.** Type uses `cqmin` (set up in the template) so it survives a 9:16 or 4K export. Nothing smaller than ~1.6cqmin. - **Honest scales.** Bar/area baselines start at 0. If you must truncate an axis, say so. ## Color & palette - Single-series / emphasis: `var(--accent)`. - Categorical: `var(--c1)` … `var(--c6)` in order (already tuned for light & dark). - Sequential (heat/intensity): interpolate opacity of one hue, e.g. `rgba(79,70,229,<0..1>)`. - Keep fills calm; reserve high saturation for the one thing you want noticed. --- ## KPI scorecard A row of big-number cards. Best first thing the eye hits; pairs well above a chart. ```html
Daily · X
3,892
▲ 12% vs prev
LinkedIn
9,149
▲ 4%
``` Drop the `.delta` line if there's no comparison. Size `value` down (`font-size:5cqmin`) if you need 5–6 cards. ## Bar chart — vertical Inline SVG with a 0-baseline, light gridlines, and value labels on top. Scale bar heights to your data's max. ```html ``` Compute in your head or with a quick script: `height = round(value / maxValue * 450)`, `y = 490 - height`. Keep `rx` small (4–8) for a modern look. ## Bar chart — horizontal / ranking Better than vertical when labels are long or you're ranking many items. Bars grow rightward from a left baseline; put the label and value on the bar. ```html ``` When the value label won't fit inside a short bar, place it just to the right of the bar end instead (as in the second row). ## Grouped bars For several series across periods (the daily/weekly/monthly shape). Cluster bars per period; one color per series; a small legend. Keep ≤3 series per cluster or switch to small multiples (one mini-chart per series). ```html ``` ## Line / area chart For trends over time. Build a polyline from points; add a soft area fill below; label the latest point directly. ```html ``` For multiple lines, repeat `polyline` with `--c1/--c2/…` and label each at its right end (no legend needed when lines are labeled directly). ## Donut / pie Parts of a whole, ≤6 slices. Donut (with a hole) reads cleaner than a full pie and leaves room for a center total. Use `stroke-dasharray` on circles — no path math. ```html ``` `dash = round(value/total * 1131)`; each slice's `dashoffset = -(sum of previous dashes)`. Add a small legend with the same `--cN` swatches. ## Scatter Two-variable relationship. Plot circles; optionally size them for a third variable (bubble). ```html ``` ## Data table Rows of structured records. Use the template's `table.data`; right-align numbers with `.num`; bold or tint the standout row. ```html
PlatformDailyWeeklyMonthly
X — CopilotKit3,89233,613162,176
X — Atai1,39720,352595,670
LinkedIn — CopilotKit9,14920,34963,500
``` Add a subtle zebra (`tr:nth-child(even){background:var(--bg-0)}`) only for long tables. ## Process / flow diagram Nodes + connectors for a pipeline, flow, or architecture. Rounded rects + arrowhead marker. ```html ``` For branches/loops, route connectors with `` and reuse the `#arrow` marker. ## Timeline A sequence of dated events along a spine. ```html ``` ## Composing a dashboard When the input has multiple natural cuts (e.g. Daily / Weekly / Monthly × platforms), make **one composed layout**, not three loose charts: 1. **Header KPI row** — the few numbers that matter most (e.g. today's headline figures). 2. **One or two charts** — a grouped-bar or small-multiples comparison for the trend across periods. 3. **Optional table** — the full grid for anyone who wants exact numbers. Lay it out with CSS grid inside `#viz`: ```html
…KPI cards…
…grouped bars (SVG)…
…donut or table…
``` This is the generative-UI instinct: one self-contained artifact that reads as a single designed thing. --- ## Escalation: Chart.js Use only when you need many data points or the *openable HTML* should be interactive. Load from CDN and **call `vizReady()` in the animation `onComplete`** so the export waits for the finished chart: ```html ``` Wrap the `` in a sized `.panel` (Chart.js needs a sized parent when `maintainAspectRatio:false`). Pull series colors from the CSS tokens so light/dark theming still works. ## Escalation: Three.js For genuine 3D. Load `three` from CDN, render one frame (or a slow loop), and call `vizReady()` after the first frame is drawn. A static export captures a single frame, so compose the camera angle deliberately. This is rarely the right tool for data — reserve it for spatial/3D subjects. --- ## render.mjs flag reference ``` node /scripts/render.mjs --in index.html --out out.png [flags] ``` | Flag | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `--in ` | — | Input HTML (required) | | `--out ` | `.png` | Output PNG path (dirs auto-created) | | `--aspect ` | `16:9` | `16:9` `4:3` `1:1` `9:16` `21:9` `3:2` `2:1` | | `--width ` | `1600` | With `--aspect`: sets size from width. With `--height`: exact. | | `--height ` | from aspect | With `--aspect`: sets size from height. With `--width`: exact. | | `--scale ` | `2` | Device pixel ratio (2 = retina-crisp; 3 for print) | | `--theme ` | OS | `light` or `dark` (passed to the page as `?theme=`) | | `--bg ` | `white` | `white`, `transparent`, or `#rrggbb` | | `--wait ` | `8000` | Max wait for the page's `__VIZ_READY__` signal | Common sizes: 16:9 → 1600×900 (default), 1920×1080 (`--width 1920`), 4K (`--width 3840`). Square 1080 (`--aspect 1:1 --width 1080`). Vertical story 1080×1920 (`--aspect 9:16 --width 1080`). The renderer tries Playwright (installed Chrome → Edge → bundled Chromium), then a system Chrome/Chromium/Edge/Brave binary. If all fail it prints the one-time install command.
